LayerNorm computes statistics independently across each example’s final feature axis. Backward subtracts the mean upstream scaled gradient and its projection onto the normalized input, then multiplies by inverse standard deviation. Weight and bias gradients reduce over every leading axis. The cache stores the forward weight as well as normalized activations, so accidental weight mutation cannot change that backward calculation. The reference supports one outstanding forward call at a time.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** For upstream scaled gradient $u=g\odot\gamma$, normalized input $\hat x$, and inverse standard deviation $r$, $\nabla_xL=r[u-\operatorname{mean}(u)-\hat x\operatorname{mean}(u\hat x)]$. Means are over normalized features only. Sum affine-parameter gradients over leading dimensions, and test constant inputs where epsilon controls the result. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07467)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://theaisummer.com/normalization/) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html).
